Features.title: Bookmarks that organize themselves
Features.description: WakeMark syncs your X bookmarks, tags them by topic, sorts them into lists, and turns them into digests that arrive on your schedule. No setup, no manual sorting.

TextReveal.text: " Your X/Tweet bookmarks, finally organized, summarized, and understood "

items.question: How do you access my bookmarks? Do I need to share my X/Twitter password?
items.answer: No. You connect through X/Twitter's official OAuth flow, which gives WakeMark read-only access to your bookmarks. We never see your password, and you can revoke access anytime from your X/Twitter settings.

items.question: What happens to my data if I cancel?
items.answer: Your bookmarks and lists remain yours. If you cancel, you keep everything you've already synced, and you can resubscribe anytime to pick up where you left off.

items.question: How is WakeMark different from saving tweets to Notion or Readwise?
items.answer: Those tools store links. WakeMark reads, categorizes, and summarizes your bookmarks for you. You get topic-based auto-tagging, shareable themed lists, and a digest that surfaces what matters instead of creating another pile of unread saves.

items.question: What does AI auto-tagging actually do?
items.answer: When your bookmarks sync, our AI reads each one and assigns topic tags such as "startup fundraising," "CSS layout," or "machine learning." There is nothing to configure: tags appear automatically, ready for filtering, searching, and list-building.

items.question: Is there a free trial?
items.answer: Yes. Every account starts with a 7-day free trial. After that, plans start at $59/year, depending on when you join. Your price is locked in for as long as you stay subscribed, and you can cancel anytime.

items.question: How often do bookmarks sync?
items.answer: Bookmarks sync automatically every day, and you can trigger a manual sync whenever you want. There is no bookmark limit.

items.question: What does the email digest look like?
items.answer: It is a clean summary of your recent bookmarks, grouped by topic. Each entry includes the key takeaway in a sentence or two, along with a direct link to the original tweet. Think of it as a personal briefing, not a wall of links.

items.question: Could X/Twitter block this or change its API?
items.answer: We use X/Twitter's official API within its published rate limits. If X/Twitter changes something on its end, we adapt. Bookmarks already synced to WakeMark remain safe regardless of what happens with the API.
